enonce.texte:
Transform the following direct statements into reported speech. Use the introductory verb said and make the necessary tense changes.

  1. "I am tired," she said.
  2. "We have finished our homework," they said.
  3. "I will call you tomorrow," he said.
  4. "I can speak French," she said.
  5. "They are leaving now," he said.
  6. "I have never been to London," she said.

questions.texte: Transform the direct statements into reported speech.
questions.reponse: 1. She said that she was tired. 2. They said that they had finished their homework. 3. He said that he would call me the next day. 4. She said that she could speak French. 5. He said that they were leaving then. 6. She said that she had never been to London.

sousQuestions.texte: Explain the tense changes from direct to reported speech.
sousQuestions.reponse: Present simple → past simple; present perfect → past perfect; will → would; can → could; present continuous → past continuous.

enonce.texte:
Transform the following direct questions into reported speech. Use asked or wanted to know.

  1. "Do you speak English?" she asked me.
  2. "Where are you going?" he asked.
  3. "Have you ever visited Cameroon?" they asked.
  4. "What time does the train leave?" she asked.
  5. "Are you coming to the party?" he asked her.
  6. "Why did you leave early?" she asked.

questions.texte: Transform the direct questions into reported speech.
questions.reponse: 1. She asked me if I spoke English. 2. He asked where I was going. 3. They asked if I had ever visited Cameroon. 4. She asked what time the train left. 5. He asked her if she was coming to the party. 6. She asked why I had left early.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the word order for reported questions?
sousQuestions.reponse: Reported questions use statement word order (subject + verb), not question word order. For yes/no questions, use 'if' or 'whether'.

enonce.texte:
Complete the sentences with said or told in the correct form.

  1. She _______ me that she was happy.
  2. He _______ he would arrive late.
  3. They _______ us the news yesterday.
  4. I _______ you not to worry.
  5. She _______ that she had finished the project.
  6. He _______ me his name.

questions.reponse: 1. told, 2. said, 3. told, 4. told, 5. said, 6. told

sousQuestions.texte: When do we use 'say' and when do we use 'tell'?
sousQuestions.reponse: We use 'say' without a personal object (she said that...). We use 'tell' with a personal object (she told me that...).

enonce.texte:
Transform the following commands and requests into reported speech. Use appropriate introductory verbs like told, asked, ordered, or advised.

  1. "Close the door," she said to me.
  2. "Please help me," he asked her.
  3. "Don't be late," my mother said to me.
  4. "Could you open the window?" he asked.
  5. "Stop talking!" the teacher ordered.
  6. "You should see a doctor," she advised me.

questions.texte: Transform the commands and requests into reported speech.
questions.reponse: 1. She told me to close the door. 2. He asked her to help him. 3. My mother told me not to be late. 4. He asked me to open the window. 5. The teacher ordered us to stop talking. 6. She advised me to see a doctor.

sousQuestions.texte: How do we report negative commands?
sousQuestions.reponse: We use 'not to + infinitive'. Example: 'She told me not to be late.'

enonce.texte:
Transform the following sentences into reported speech using an appropriate reporting verb: explain, suggest, promise, warn, advise, or offer.

  1. "You should apply for the job," she said to me.
  2. "I will definitely help you," he said.
  3. "Let's go to the cinema," she said.
  4. "Be careful with that knife," he said to me.
  5. "The project will be finished by Friday," the manager said.
  6. "I can carry your bag for you," he said.

questions.texte: Transform the sentences into reported speech using advanced reporting verbs.
questions.reponse: 1. She advised me to apply for the job. 2. He promised to help me. 3. She suggested going to the cinema. 4. He warned me to be careful with the knife. 5. The manager explained that the project would be finished by Friday. 6. He offered to carry my bag.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the difference between 'suggest' and 'advise' in reported speech?
sousQuestions.reponse: 'Suggest' is often used with a gerund (suggest doing) or a that-clause (suggest that we go). 'Advise' is used with an object + infinitive (advise me to do).

enonce.texte:
You are a journalist. Transform the following interview into a news report using reported speech.

Interview transcript:

Journalist: "What is your opinion on the new education policy?"

Minister: "I believe it will improve the quality of education in Cameroon."

Journalist: "Will the government increase the budget for schools?"

Minister: "Yes, we are planning to allocate more resources to education."

Journalist: "When will the new policy be implemented?"

Minister: "We will start implementing it next year."

questions.texte: Write a news report summarizing this interview using reported speech.
questions.reponse: The journalist asked the Minister about his opinion on the new education policy. The Minister said that he believed it would improve the quality of education in Cameroon. When asked if the government would increase the budget for schools, the Minister confirmed that they were planning to allocate more resources to education. He also stated that they would start implementing the policy next year.

enonce.texte:
You had a phone conversation with a client. Write a professional email to your boss reporting what was discussed. Use reported speech.

Key points from the conversation:

  • "I am interested in your services."
  • "We need a proposal by next Friday."
  • "The budget is around $10,000."
  • "I will send you the requirements tomorrow."
  • "Could you send me a sample contract?"

questions.texte: Write a professional email reporting the conversation to your boss.
questions.reponse:
Subject: Report of Conversation with Client

Dear Sir,

I am writing to report on my conversation with the client today. The client expressed interest in our services and said that they needed a proposal by next Friday. He mentioned that the budget is around $10,000. He told me that he would send the requirements tomorrow. Additionally, he asked if we could send him a sample contract.

I will prepare the documents accordingly.

Yours sincerely,
[Your Name]

enonce.texte:
Find and correct the errors in these reported speech sentences.

  1. She said me that she was going to the market.
  2. He asked that I was feeling better.
  3. They told that they had finished the work.
  4. She asked me where was the station.
  5. He suggested to go to the restaurant.
  6. The teacher said us to study harder.

questions.texte: Find and correct the mistakes in each sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. She told me that she was going to the market. 2. He asked if I was feeling better. 3. They said that they had finished the work. / They told me that they had finished the work. 4. She asked me where the station was. 5. He suggested going to the restaurant. / He suggested that we go to the restaurant. 6. The teacher told us to study harder.

enonce.texte: Write a short story (150-200 words) about a memorable conversation you had with someone. Use at least eight different examples of reported speech in your story. Include a mix of statements, questions, commands, and advanced reporting verbs.

questions.texte: Write a story using various forms of reported speech.
questions.reponse: Example: 'Last year, I had an inspiring conversation with my grandfather. He told me that he had lived in Douala for 40 years. He explained how the city had changed over time. I asked him what his favorite memory was. He said that he remembered the independence celebration vividly. He warned me not to forget our family traditions. He advised me to always help others. My grandmother suggested cooking a special meal to celebrate his memories. She promised to teach me the recipe. When I thanked them, they said they were happy to share their stories. My grandfather asked if I would pass on these traditions to my children. I promised that I would. That conversation reminded me of the importance of family.'

enonce.texte:
Transform the following direct sentences into reported speech. Pay attention to the time expressions that need to change.

  1. "I will see you tomorrow," she said.
  2. "We went to the beach yesterday," they said.
  3. "I am going to the market now," he said.
  4. "She has worked here for five years," the manager said.
  5. "I need to finish this today," she said.
  6. "We are meeting them next week," he said.

questions.texte: Transform the sentences into reported speech with appropriate time expression changes.
questions.reponse: 1. She said that she would see me the next day. 2. They said that they had gone to the beach the day before. 3. He said that he was going to the market then. 4. The manager said that she had worked there for five years. 5. She said that she needed to finish that that day. 6. He said that they were meeting them the following week.

sousQuestions.texte: What changes do we make to time expressions in reported speech?
sousQuestions.reponse: today → that day; tomorrow → the next day; yesterday → the day before / the previous day; now → then; next week → the following week.
